RESPONDENTS (BY SRI. RAVISH BENNI., ADVOCATE FOR R-2;
 R-1 IS SERVED AND UNREPRESENTED)

THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:29.12.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.864/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE,MEMBER, ADDITIONAL MACT, KUNDAPURA,
ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE N S SANJAY GOWDA
ORAL JUDGMENT
1. An accident occurred on 14.06.2016 as a result of which the claimant suffered injuries.
2. The claimant approached the Tribunal seeking compensation and the insurer entered appearance and as usual denied all the averments.

3. The Tribunal on assessment of the evidence has come to the conclusion the accident did occur as a result of rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle and, it thereafter proceeded to fasten NC: 2024:KHC:51212 liability on the insurer and ordered the payment of compensation of Rs.6,31,837/-.
4.
Both the insurer and the claimant are in appeal.
5. The insurer contends that the claimant himself was riding the motorcycle, contrary to his version in the claim petition that he was a pillion rider.
It is therefore contended that since he himself had contributed to the accident and the accident was a result of negligence, no compensation can be payable.

6. In the alternative, it is submitted that, assuming that the insurer is liable to pay compensation,
contributory negligence is attributed to the claimant.

7. As far as this aspect is concerned, it is not in dispute that the vehicle was covered with a package policy and, therefore, the rider of the motorcycle and the pillion rider would be covered so long as the rider was not the insured.

Admittedly, in this case, the NC: 2024:KHC:51212 claimant was not the insured and it really does not matter as to whether he was a pillion rider or a rider of the motorcycle, because as long as the motorcycle was covered with the policy of insurance and an Sri Dinesh Naik vs Sri Madeva G Naik on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142630605/
3 accident occurred, the insurer would be liable to pay the compensation.
8.

sentences.text: As far as the argument that the claimant himself contributed to the accident is concerned, it is to be stated here that the Police have not laid any charge sheet against the claimant.
The insurer has also not produced any evidence to indicate in what manner the claimant was negligent.
In the absence of any evidence to establish this negligence on the part of the claimant, this argument cannot be accepted.
9. As far as compensation is concerned, the claimant had suffered fracture of both bones (Tibia and Fibula) of his right leg and had a laceration.
The doctor was examined and stated that he had suffered a disability to the extent of 28%.
In my view, since the claimant NC: 2024:KHC:51212 had suffered only a fracture of the Tibia and Fibula, it would be appropriate to treat the whole body disability at 15%.
10. As far as the notional income is concerned, the Tribunal has adopted a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month, since there was no evidence to that effect.

As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined the notional income as Rs.9,500/- for the accident of the year 2016, it would be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.9,500/-.

Consequently, towards 'loss of future earning' the claimant would be entitled to Rs.2,73,600/- (Rs.9,500/- X 12 X 16 X 15%).
11.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.59,557/-
towards medical expenses and Rs.16,000/- towards future medical expenses.
These sums are just improper and are accordingly affirmed.
12. The Tribunal has awarded has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' and NC: 2024:KHC:51212 Rs.50,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
These sums are also just and proper and hence are affirmed.
13. The Tribunal has taken the laid-up period as 9 months.

In my view for a fracture of both the bones i.e., Tibia and Fibula, it would be appropriate to treat the laid-up period as only 6 months and, accordingly, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.57,000/- (Rs.9,500/- X 6 months)
towards 'loss of income' during the laid-up period'.
14.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.9,600/-
towards 'transportation expenses' and Rs.25,000/- towards 'food and nourishment'.
Since the claimant was hospitalized for 9 days, the sums awarded by the Tribunal cannot be found fault with.
15. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:
